stories.headline: KENNEDY OPPOSES QUOTAS FOR JOBS ON BASIS OF RACE; Says Education Is Greatest Need of Negroes--Doubts U.S. Can 'Repair Past' RIGHTS BILLS PRESSED Congress Urged to Act This Session--Election Year Pressure in '64 Cited Calls Education Vital KENNEDY OPPOSES RACIAL JOB QUOTA Protests Illustrate Plight
stories.summary: President John F. Kennedy opposes job quotas based on race, instead emphasizing education as the greatest need for African Americans, during a news conference. He doubts the US can 'repair the past' through such measures.

stories.headline: SAC HEAD DEMURS AS JOINT CHIEFS BACK A-TEST BAN; Gen. Power Urges Senate to Reject Pact as Not Being in Best U.S. Interest LEMAY HAS MISGIVINGS Air Force Leader Says He Might Have Fought Accord Had It Not Been Signed Goldwater Protests SAC HEAD DEMURS ON TEST BAN PACT Marines' Chief Decisive Wants Tests Continued Differ With LeMay Indicate No Pressure Had No Objection Humphrey Protests New Group Fights Treaty
stories.summary: General Curtis LeMay and other military leaders express misgivings about a proposed nuclear test ban treaty, with LeMay stating he would not have backed it had it not already been signed. Senator Barry Goldwater also protests the treaty.

stories.headline: RAILS AND UNIONS ACCEPT PROPOSAL FOR ARBITRATION; Agree to Wirtz Plan on Two Main Issues, Crew Size and Job Reduction TALKS STILL 'CRITICAL' Secretary Says Decision on Concrete Steps Remains  Meeting Today Set Interpretation a Problem RAILS AND UNIONS ACCEPT PROPOSAL Wirtz Issues Report Unions Note Acceptance Size of Board Omitted Rail Stocks Rise
stories.summary: Railroads and unions agree to submit two major issues, crew size and job reduction, to binding arbitration, following a proposal by Secretary Wirtz. The decision is seen as a critical step towards resolving labor disputes.

stories.headline: ANTI-U.S. FEELING RISES IN VIETNAM AS UNREST GROWS; Nhu's Power in Regime Gains --Harder Line Toward Washington Is Feared 30 DEATHS REPORTED Troops Arrest Professors and May Seize Students to Avert a Rebellion Killing at Hue Indicated Regime Accuses Reds Anti-American Feeling Grows in Vietnam After Regime Acts Against Buddhists SAIGON STUDENTS REPORTED UNEASY Humiliation of U.S. Citizens Continues as Nhu Gains Power in Government Mrs. Nhu Exuberant Humiliations Continue Lodge Sees Two Buddhists
stories.summary: Anti-US sentiment grows in Vietnam as the government, led by Nhu, takes a harder line towards Washington, with reports of arrests, killings, and humiliation of US citizens. The regime accuses communists of fueling the unrest.

rounds.blurb: President John F. Kennedy opposed job quotas based on race, emphasizing education instead. The US military leadership expressed misgivings about a proposed nuclear test ban treaty. Labor disputes between railroads and unions progressed with an agreement to arbitration.

stories.headline: FIVE DAYS LATER FROM EUROPE.; THE JURA OFF CAPE RACE. Sympathy of the Workingmen of Manchester with the North.A Congratulatory Address to President Lincoln. HIS EMANCIPATION POLICY APPROVED.Increase of 2,392,000 in theBritish Revenue.Additional French Troops Wanted in Mexico. GREAT BRITAIN. FRANCE. GREECE. Commercial News by the Jura. LATEST VIA LONDONDERRY.
stories.summary: Workingmen in Manchester express sympathy with the North and approve of President Lincoln's emancipation policy, as reported by a steamship from Liverpool

stories.headline: IMPORTANT DOCUMENTS; An Inside View of the Affairs of the Rebel Government. The Correspondence Intercepted by Our Blockaders Off Charleston Letters from the Rebel Secretary of State, Secretary of the Treasury, and Secretary of the Navy. How Money is Raised in England by the Hypothecation of Cotton. How Iron-Clods are Built for the Rebels. Our Neutral English Cousins Who Furnish Rebel Supplies. Exaggeration of the Rebel Suecessesin Virginia.DESPONDENCY AT BRAGG'S FAILURE. INTERCEPTED REBEL DISPATCHES CORRESPONDENCE OF CONFEDERATE TREASURY AND NAVY DEPARTMENTS.
stories.summary: Correspondence between Confederate officials, including Benjamin and Memminger, is intercepted by Union blockaders off Charleston, revealing details about the Rebel government's affairs

stories.headline: Does the War Promote a Pro-Slavery Reaction?; The French in Mexico
stories.summary: The war raises questions about a potential pro-slavery reaction, while French forces are active in Mexico

stories.headline: TRUTH FROM RICHMOND.
stories.summary: A Richmond newspaper discusses the necessity of conscription, highlighting the challenges faced by the Confederacy during the war

rounds.blurb: President Lincoln's emancipation policy was approved by workingmen in Manchester. The Union blockaders intercepted correspondence between Confederate officials, revealing details about the Rebel government's affairs. The Confederacy faced challenges, including the necessity of conscription.

stories.headline: 2 STUDENTS IN COLORADO SCHOOL SAID TO GUN DOWN AS MANY AS 23 AND KILL THEMSELVES IN A SIEGE
stories.summary: Two students, Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold, carried out a deadly shooting at Columbine High School, killing and injuring many before taking their own lives, in a violent incident that targeted minorities and athletes. The attack occurred during a time of growing concern about school violence.

stories.headline: CRISIS IN THE BALKANS: THE ROAD TO WAR -- A special report.; How a President, Distracted by Scandal, Entered Balkan War
stories.summary: President Clinton's handling of the Balkan crisis has been questioned, with some arguing that his impeachment hearings distracted him from fully addressing the issue, as he relied on his top aides to navigate the situation. The crisis in Yugoslavia presented a significant foreign policy challenge for the administration.

stories.headline: Allies' Progress Remains Unclear as Few Details Are Made Public
stories.summary: NATO's military progress in Yugoslavia is unclear due to a lack of detailed reports, despite claims of steady dismantling of Belgrade's war-making powers, as ethnic cleansing by Serb forces in Kosovo continues. The situation remains uncertain as the allied air attacks enter their second week.

stories.headline: The Low-Budget Realities Of Making Indie Films; A Hollywood Director Takes Off on His Own, Even if He Can't Get His Movie Distributed
stories.summary: Hollywood director Phil Joanou is making his debut in the independent film world with his low-budget movie Entropy, which will open the Los Angeles Independent Film Festival, highlighting the challenges of distributing independent films despite backing from major companies. The film showcases the realities of indie filmmaking.

rounds.blurb: The Columbine High School shooting occurred, claiming many lives. President Clinton faced challenges in addressing the Balkan crisis amidst impeachment hearings. NATO's air attacks in Yugoslavia continued, targeting Serb forces.
